concepts.gloss: The algebra isomorphism that places a cyclic convolution of pairwise coprime length S on a product of cyclic axes, so that the change of coefficient order is a sequence of controlled shifts.

concepts.name: Sort-free Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Gaussian resampling in which the source and target coordinate permutations remain inside the transform formula, so they are never executed as separate full sorts.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity

concepts.name: Permutation cancellation

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing
concepts.gloss: Encoding a polynomial with signed integer coefficients as a single integer by placing the coefficients at fixed bit spacing, so that one integer product computes the polynomial product.

evidence.quote: packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A transform over the polynomial ring in which the roots of unity are powers of y, so that multiplying by a root is a signed shift of a coefficient list, computed with radix-two butterflies.

evidence.quote: synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle

concepts.name: Phase twist to negacyclic wrap
concepts.gloss: A phase multiplication of the last cyclic coordinate that turns the cyclic wrap-around into the negative wrap of the polynomial ring, so that the original cyclic product is recovered once the twist is removed.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial

evidence.quote: Convolution from the retained transform layout

concepts.name: Rounding and carry recovery
concepts.gloss: The step that removes the known normalizations and digit scales, rounds each recovered coefficient (with error below 1/2), and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product.

evidence.quote: propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product

concepts.name: Transform pipeline for integer product

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost accounting
concepts.gloss: The fixing of rational exponents, including τ = σ = 1 − 2^−50 and κ = 2^−182, so that every term of the cost table is within the bound O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) after division by the stored volume V.

evidence.quote: makes all terms in its cost table fit

concepts.name: Sub-linearithmic integer multiplication on a fixed tape machine
aliases: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.gloss: A single deterministic fixed-alphabet machine with a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) worst-case time, with κ = 2^−182, disproving the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: The logarithm to base b is the inverse of the exponential b^x, satisfying log(xy) = log x + log y and log(x^c) = c log x, with lg denoting the base-2 logarithm and ln the natural logarithm.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The floor ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling ⌈x⌉ is the smallest integer not less than x.

concepts.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
concepts.gloss: For a ratio r different from 1, the finite sum 1 + r + … + r^(k−1) equals (r^k − 1)/(r − 1).

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: Induction proves a statement for every integer n at least n0 by proving it for n0 and proving it for n from its truth for smaller values (strong induction) or for the previous value (weak induction).

concepts.name: Recurrence relations for running times
concepts.gloss: A recurrence defines a cost T(n) in terms of costs at smaller sizes, and is solved by unrolling it into a sum or by substituting a guessed bound and checking it by induction.

concepts.name: Cartesian product of sets
concepts.gloss: The Cartesian product A_1 × … × A_t is the set of ordered tuples (a_1, …, a_t) with each a_i in A_i.

concepts.name: Permutation of a finite set
concepts.gloss: A permutation of a finite set is a bijection from that set to itself, and permutations can be composed and inverted.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficients
concepts.gloss: The binomial coefficient binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set and equals n!/(k!(n−k)!).

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: Tuples are ordered lexicographically by comparing their entries at the first position where they differ, so the row-major order of an array is the lexicographic order of its index pairs.

concepts.name: Graphs, vertices and edges
concepts.gloss: A graph consists of a set of vertices and a set of edges, each edge joining two vertices, and two vertices are adjacent when an edge joins them.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
concepts.gloss: a ≡ b (mod m) means that m divides a − b, arithmetic on residue classes modulo m is well defined, and a has an inverse modulo m exactly when gcd(a, m) = 1.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprime integers
concepts.gloss: The gcd of a and b is the largest integer dividing both, two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1, and the extended Euclidean algorithm finds integers x and y with ax + by = gcd(a, b).

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer p at least 2 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p, and every integer at least 2 is a product of primes in exactly one way up to order.

concepts.name: Division with remainder
concepts.gloss: For integers a and b > 0 there are unique integers q and r with a = bq + r and 0 ≤ r < b, and then q = ⌊a/b⌋.

concepts.name: Limits of sequences and functions
aliases: limit as n tends to infinity
concepts.gloss: A quantity f(n) tends to L as n tends to infinity when, for every ε > 0, |f(n) − L| is less than ε for all sufficiently large n.

concepts.name: Nth roots of unity and polar form
concepts.gloss: The complex numbers z with z^n = 1 are e^(2πik/n) for k = 0, …, n−1, and Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ gives every nonzero complex number the polar form r·e^(iθ).

concepts.name: Vector spaces, bases and linear maps
concepts.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication by a field of scalars, a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and a linear map is a function between vector spaces that preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

concepts.name: Matrices, inverses and triangular matrices
concepts.gloss: A matrix records a linear map relative to chosen bases, matrix products correspond to composition of maps, an invertible matrix has an inverse, and a lower- or upper-triangular matrix has all entries on one side of the diagonal equal to zero.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
concepts.gloss: A scalar λ is an eigenvalue of a square matrix M when Mv = λv for some nonzero vector v, and such a v is an eigenvector for λ.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and elementary row operations
concepts.gloss: Gaussian elimination reduces a matrix by adding multiples of rows to other rows and swapping or scaling rows, and it writes an invertible matrix as a product of elementary matrices.

concepts.name: Dot product and orthogonality
concepts.gloss: The dot product of x and y in R^n is the sum of the products x_i y_i, and two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.

concepts.name: Indicator vector of a subset
concepts.gloss: For a subset T of a finite index set, its indicator vector has entry 1 at the positions of the elements of T and entry 0 at all other positions.

concepts.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and XOR
concepts.gloss: Addition of bits is the exclusive-or operation, so 1 + 1 = 0, and the integers modulo 2 form the field F_2 with two elements.

concepts.name: Dyadic rational numbers
concepts.gloss: A dyadic rational is a number m/2^k with integers m and k, equivalently a rational number with a finite binary expansion.

concepts.name: Positional (radix) notation
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer n is written in base b as n = Σ d_j b^j with digits 0 ≤ d_j < b, and binary notation is the case b = 2.

concepts.name: Two's-complement integers
concepts.gloss: A w-bit two's-complement word represents the signed integers from −2^(w−1) to 2^(w−1) − 1, with its leading bit carrying weight −2^(w−1).

background.summary: The reader has the standard undergraduate computer science core: discrete mathematics (Cartesian products, permutations, induction, binomial coefficients, graphs, modular arithmetic, gcd, primes and division with remainder), linear algebra over the real and rational numbers (vector spaces, bases, matrices, eigenvalues, dot products, Gaussian elimination), calculus-level analysis (logarithms, exponentials, limits, geometric sums, roots of unity and Euler's formula), and algorithms and computer organization (Omega, Theta and little-o notation, recurrences, positional notation, two's-complement words). Not assumed are fields other than F_2, tensor products, bilinear forms, Gaussian integers, rings and groups, the integer Chinese remainder theorem, limit inferior and Newton iteration.
